idiom_name: std::identity — transparent constexpr pass-through function object (<functional>, C++20)
implementation_notes: Since C++20, <functional> ships std::identity — a constexpr, empty function object whose operator()(T&& t) returns std::forward<T>(t); its nested is_transparent tag marks it as a transparent comparator/projection, and it is the default projection of the ranges algorithms, so the classic no-op strategy class collapses into a one-type pass-through (on C++14/17 toolchains a generic forwarding lambda [](auto&& x) -> decltype(auto) { return std::forward<decltype(x)>(x); } is the same idiom). Template parameters and auto&& callables replace the strategy-object machinery; the classic runtime-dispatch form is still justified when callables must cross separately compiled translation units — but wrap the identity in std::function only there, because type erasure re-introduces an indirect call and a possible allocation.
pitfalls: Wrapping the identity in std::function for storage re-introduces type erasure: an indirect (virtual) call and possibly a heap allocation per invocation, defeating inlining in hot paths; pass std::identity{} or a template/auto&& parameter instead.

Value-category loss: a by-value generic lambda [](auto x){ return x; } copies or moves its argument and returns a decayed prvalue, so chained transforms silently move-from the input; std::identity's forwarding-reference operator() preserves lvalue/rvalue-ness — hand-rolled identities need auto&& plus decltype(auto).

operator() returns T&&: forwarding the result out of a wider scope (storing it in a member, returning it from a longer-lived helper) dangles once the argument dies; identity forwards value category, it does not extend lifetimes.

C++ has no binary identity: in comparator contexts the neutral form is the default projection (or std::less<>{} on the raw values); a wrong-arity callable surfaces as pages of template diagnostics deep inside the algorithm, not as a type error at the call site.
Name-lookup trap: std::identity (values, <functional>) is unrelated to std::type_identity (types, <type_traits>); confusing the two yields compile errors, not pass-through behaviour.

variants.name: Generic forwarding lambda (pre-C++20)
variants.implementation_notes: Before std::identity existed, a generic lambda with forwarding references was (and remains) the zero-dependency idiom: an empty closure type, fully inlineable, no allocation. Use it on C++14/17 toolchains or to keep <functional> out of the translation unit; semantics match std::identity exactly, but it carries no is_transparent tag, so transparent heterogeneous lookup must be enabled by the comparator type itself.
